speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you've presented with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you describe exactly how the skin lesions look and where they are located on your body? Have you recently had any insect bites or been exposed to animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given your camping trip and the self-resolving knee pain, could you describe the appearance of the skin lesions on your wrist and tell me if they are itchy or painful? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or stiffness in your left knee now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erysipeloid (Caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, likely acquired from handling fish or animals during camping)
